scope: Email history case semantics and quoted local parts
findings: Smith@example.com and smith@example.com collapse to one record; Smith@ then recalls lowercase address. Host semantics may distinguish these mailboxes.
dev@INFO.example is not recalled by dev@info; storing both yields two records for case-equivalent domains. Ordinary EXAMPLE/example control matches and merges.
All three quoted-local-part inputs lose opening quote; quoted whitespace additionally fragments the address.
Plus-tag variants remain distinct; four surface controls preserve plus, dots and address literals.
source_scope: SMTP preserves local-part case though case-sensitive mailboxes are discouraged; domains case-insensitive; quoted local-part permits spaces. Not a claim these synthetic mailboxes exist or all providers distinguish case.
causes: Same TurkishText.key component-unaware normalization as URL round123.
Same whitespace/token-edge normalization family as rounds124/130.
limits: Core history only, not automatic correction or actual email sending.
11 targeted scenarios; not an overall email failure rate.
